 Judgment
Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of both counsel, it is taken up for final disposal.

This is petitioners' appeal filed under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'the Act')
seeking enhancement of compensation granted for the death of Basavaraj Pujari in a motor vehicles accident dated 31.01.2018.
2.
For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
3. Petitioners are the wife, daughter and widowed sister of deceased-Basavaraj Pujari.
It is the case of the petitioners' that on 31.01.2018 at about 3:00 p.m. deceased was proceeding on motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-U-8174 ('motorcycle' for short).

On Kolhar- B.Bagewadi road, near Bannihalla bridge, an auto rickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-29-B-0798 ('offending vehicle' for short),
came in a high speed, in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased.
As a result of the accident, deceased sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.
As the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

4. Respondent Nos.1 and 2 have filed separate written statement denying that accident occurred due to rash or driving of the offending vehicle, the age, occupation, income of the deceased and also that petitioners were dependent on him.

Respondent No.2 has further averred that since the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid driving licence, it is not liable to pay the compensation and Renuka And Ors vs Lalu And Anr on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76900411/
2 prays to dismiss the petition.
5.

sentences.text: Based on these pleadings, the Tribunal framed necessary issues.

6. On behalf of petitioners, petitioner No.1 is examined as PW.1 and one witness as PW.2 and they have relied upon Exs.P1 to 7.
7.
On behalf of respondent No.2, RW.1 is examined and Exs.R1 is marked.

8. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the petition and quantified the compensation at Rs.11,34,130/- with interest at 6% per annum and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same.

9. The details of the compensation granted are as under:
 Sl. Head Amount awarded  No.
 1. Loss of dependency Rs.10,24,128/-

2. Towards loss of spousal, Rs.80,000/-
 parental and filial consortium

3 . Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-
 4. Towards transportation and Rs.15,000/-
 funeral expenses
Respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award.

11. During the course of argument, learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the Tribunal has erred in considering the income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/- p.m. and failed to add future prospects.
The compensation granted under the other heads is also on the lower side and prays to allow the appeal.
12. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and award and sought for dismissal of the appeal.

13. Heard arguments and perused the records.
14.

Having regard to the fact that the respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award, the findings of the Tribunal that the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle and in the said accident, the deceased sustained injuries and died has attained finality.
15. Based on the evidence placed on record, the Tribunal has correctly taken the age of the deceased as 34 years and multiplier 16.
In the absence of proof of exact income, the Tribunal is justified in considering the income on notional basis.

Since the accident is of the year 2018, the income ought to Renuka And Ors vs Lalu And Anr on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76900411/
3 have been taken at Rs.11,750/-. instead of Rs.8,000/- p.m.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the Tribunal has not added any compensation towards loss of future prospects.

Since the deceased was aged less than 40 years, as per Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1 (Magma's case), 40% is required to be added towards loss of future (2018) 18 SCC 130 prospects.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1 (Magma's case)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the income is required to be taken at Rs.16,450/-.

The Tribunal has rightly held that petitioners have not produced any documents to show that petitioner No.3 is a widow and she was living with the deceased and therefore, considered petitioners 1 and 2 are the only dependents.
However, in respect 2-3 dependents, the deduction towards personal and living expenses is 1/3rd.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly deducted 1/3rd of the income towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and taken 2/3rd for calculating loss of dependency.
With these components, loss of dependency is Rs.16,450 x 12 x 16 x 2/3 = Rs.21,05,600/- as against Rs.10,24,128/- granted by the Tribunal.
16. The Tribunal has rightly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.40,000/- each i.e. Rs.80,000/- in favour of petitioners 1 and 2.
Similarly the Tribunal has correctly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.15,000/- each under the head loss to estate and funeral expenses (which includes transportation charges).

17. Thus, in all petitioners 1 and 2 are entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.22,15,600/-
with interest at 6% per annum as against Rs.11,34,128/- granted by the Tribunal as detailed below:
Sl. Heads Amount Amount No awarded by the awarded by  Tribunal this Court

1 . Loss of dependency Rs.10,24,128/- Rs.21,05,600/-
 2. Towards loss of Rs.80,000/- Rs.80,000/-
 spousal, parental and  filial consortium

3. Loss to estate Rs.15,000/- Rs.15,000/-
 4. Towards Rs.15,000/- Rs.15,000/-
 transportation and  funeral expenses

18 . To this extent, the impugned judgment and award is required to be modified and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
